text: Absolutely fantastic Nigerian cuisine. The jollof rice was perfectly spiced and the fried plantains were crispy outside, soft inside. Service was attentive and the atmosphere vibrant. Best Nigerian restaurant I have visited.

Beautiful ambiance and creative fusion menu. The oxtail stew was rich and tender. Slightly overpriced but the quality justifies it. Staff was knowledgeable about every dish. Would recommend for a special occasion.

Good suya but nothing exceptional. The pepper was decent, meat was a bit dry. Location is convenient near the market. Service was slow on a busy Saturday evening. Would return if nothing else is nearby.

My go-to coffee spot in Lagos. The Naija blend is smooth and bold without being bitter. Free wifi actually works and the seats are comfortable. A bit pricey compared to roadside kiosks but worth every naira.

Authentic ofada rice and stew that tastes like home cooking. The portions are generous and the price is very reasonable. Only issue is the plastic chairs are uncomfortable for long meals. The locust beans aroma is inviting!

Classic Lagos restaurant experience. The egusi soup is always consistent, rich and thick the way it should be. They never disappoint with their pounded yam. Staff has been the same for years which shows stability. Parking can be a challenge on weekends.

Disappointing experience this visit. The chicken was overcooked and dry, chips were lukewarm. Staff seemed uninterested in customer service. Better options exist nearby for the same price. Expected more from this chain.

Best pepper soup in all of Lagos! The catfish is fresh and the pepper balance is phenomenal. Hot, spicy, and served with cold maltina. This is a cultural experience, not just a meal. The owner knows every regular customer by name.

Elegant setting with excellent continental-Nigerian fusion dishes. The lamb cutlets with jollof risotto was a highlight. Wine selection is impressive for Lagos standards. Service could be faster given the price point. Great for business dinners.

Decent wings but the flavour options are limited compared to international branches. The lemon pepper was good, the hot sauce was below average. Delivery is unreliable, better to eat in. Overpriced for what you get as a mid-range Lagos diner.

Pure Lagos street food magic. The amala texture is perfect and the ewedu soup is generous with the meat. You get a full belly for 1500 naira which is rare in 2025. The plastic chairs and noise is part of the experience. Real Lagosians know this spot.

Flame grilled chicken is decent but the spice level is tame for Nigerian palate. Peri peri sauce needs to be hotter. Service was friendly though. The location in Ikeja mall is convenient. Average overall, not worth the premium over local options.

Quality has really dropped. The meat pie no longer tastes the same as the 90s version. Doughnuts were stale and overpriced. Nostalgia keeps me returning but the experience is consistently underwhelming. Needs a serious quality upgrade.

Best shawarma outside of Abuja proper. The chicken filling is well seasoned and the wrap is generous. The chili sauce is the real highlight. Long queue at lunch but moves fast. Cash only which is annoying in 2025.

Rivers State cooking at its finest. The banga soup with starch is exactly how my grandmother made it. Owner sources fresh fish from the creek every morning. Only 12 tables so arrive early. The atmosphere is homely and the price is completely fair.

Authentic Kano-style kilishi that melts in your mouth. The spice blend is a family recipe and you can taste the difference from mass-produced versions. Excellent packaging for gifts. Prices are fair for the quality. Will order online again.

Consistently late delivery. 90-minute wait for a pizza that should take 30 minutes. The pizza itself is average, nothing special about the crust. Too expensive for mediocre quality. Only ordering again if there is a serious discount.

Great beachside dining with fresh seafood. The grilled lobster was excellent but expensive. Ambiance is unbeatable on a Sunday afternoon. Service is a bit slow but the view compensates. Bring cash because POS network can be unreliable here.

Reliable fast food option when you need something quick. The chicken and chips combo is satisfying for the price. Not exceptional but consistent. Cleanliness has improved in recent months. Good for a quick office lunch not a special outing.

Unique cultural experience combining good food with jazz music and a bookshop. The coconut rice is delicious. Great place to spend a Sunday afternoon. Slow service is part of the vibe here. The curated playlist alone is worth the visit.

Modern take on traditional Nigerian buka concept. Clean environment, transparent pricing, and genuine Nigerian flavours. The vegetable soup with assorted meat is a winner. Slightly pricier than roadside bukas but the hygiene justifies it.

Hotel restaurant with standard Nigerian buffet. Food quality varies by visit, sometimes excellent sometimes average. The fried rice is usually good. Pricing is fair for a hotel setting. Better alternatives exist for standalone dining in Ibadan.

Decent fried chicken at a reasonable price point. The skin is crispy and the seasoning is solid. Chips can sometimes be soggy. Queue management is poor during lunch rush. Good value option for students and young professionals.

Cross River State cuisine done beautifully. The Afang soup is incredibly rich and the goat meat is tender. Edikang Ikong was thick and flavourful. Chef clearly trained in Calabar. Rare to find authentic Cross River cooking in Lagos. Highly recommended.

Reliable spot for consistently good Nigerian dishes. The menu is focused which ensures quality. Excellent moi moi and the suya starter is generous. Air conditioning works properly. Can get crowded on Fridays but worth the wait.

Premium experience with outstanding cocktails. The intercontinental menu has excellent Nigerian-inspired options. Great for celebrating milestones. Service is polished and professional. The chicken suya bruschetta fusion starter was creative and delicious.

The real deal. Hausa mallam who has been grilling on this corner for 15 years. The suya spice is made fresh daily, the beef is lean and properly trimmed. Newspaper wrapping is part of the experience. Come before 9pm or it will finish.

Standard fast food experience. Chicken is reliably crispy though the spice level is mild for Nigerian taste. The coleslaw is fresh. Value for money is fair. Better for a quick bite than a sit-down meal. Consistent if not exciting.

Excellent fresh fish selection with beautiful waterfront setting. The catfish pepper soup was outstanding and properly hot. Tilapia grilled with Nigerian spices was tender. Service can be slow but the fish quality makes it worthwhile. Weekend dining spot.

Solid fried chicken that rivals the bigger chains at half the price. The puff puff is fresh and the zobo drink is homemade and delicious. Very popular with university students. No pretension, just genuinely good food at honest prices.
